plants.name: Euphorbia pulcherrima
plants.description: A shrub with showy colored bracts surrounding small yellow true flowers. In its native range it can grow to several meters tall, and it is widely grown as a potted plant and in frost-free gardens during the holiday season.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late autumn to winter (November to February) in the Northern Hemisphere
plants.location: Native to Mexico and Central America; cultivated worldwide, especially in warm climates and as an indoor plant
plants.funFact: The colorful 'petals' are actually modified leaves called bracts, and the plant needs long nights of about 12 hours of darkness to color up.

plants.name: Camellia sasanqua
plants.description: An evergreen shrub with glossy dark green leaves and fragrant, delicate single or semi-double flowers. It blooms earlier than the common camellia and is popular for hedges and espaliers in mild climates.
plants.location: Native to southern Japan; widely grown in the southeastern United States, southern Europe, Australia, and New Zealand
plants.funFact: Oil pressed from its seeds is used in Japan for cooking and hair care, and it is related to the tea plant, Camellia sinensis.

plants.name: Delonix regia
plants.description: A broad, umbrella-shaped tree with fern-like leaves that erupts in clusters of large, vivid flowers. In the Southern Hemisphere summer it creates spectacular scarlet canopies along streets and in parks.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late spring to summer in the Southern Hemisphere (November to January)
plants.location: Native to Madagascar; cultivated in tropical and subtropical regions including Australia, South Africa, Brazil, and the Caribbean
plants.funFact: Despite being one of the most celebrated ornamental trees in the tropics, it is endangered in its native Madagascar.

plants.name: Helleborus niger
plants.description: A low-growing evergreen perennial with leathery, dark green leaves and nodding, cup-shaped flowers with golden stamens. It flowers in the cold of winter, often poking through snow.
plants.bloomingSeason: Early winter to early spring (December to March)
plants.location: Native to the mountains of central and southern Europe; cultivated in shaded gardens across temperate regions
plants.funFact: Despite its name, it is not a rose at all but a member of the buttercup family, and all parts of the plant are poisonous.
